arxiv-1709-06319.title: Hugenholtz-Pines theorem for multicomponent Bose–Einstein condensates
arxiv-1709-06319.creator: Shohei Watabe
arxiv-1709-06319.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Shohei Watabe. The Hugenholtz-Pines (HP) theorem is derived for Bose–Einstein condensates (BECs) with internal degrees of freedom. The low-energy Ward–Takahashi identity is provided in the system with the linear and quadratic symmetry breaking terms. This identity serves to organize the HP theorem for multicomponent BECs, such as the binary BEC as well as the spin- f f spinor BEC in the presence of a magnetic field with broken U ( 1 ) (1) × \times SO ( 3 ) (3) symmetry.

arxiv-2003-00973.title: Differential Privacy at Risk: Bridging Randomness and Privacy Budget
arxiv-2003-00973.creator:
ame Ashish Dandekar \email adandekar@ens.fr, 
ame Debabrota Basu \email basud@chalmers.se, 
ame Stéphane Bressan \email steph@nus.edu.sg
arxiv-2003-00973.description: Abstract The calibration of noise for a privacy-preserving mechanism depends on the sensitivity of the query and the prescribed privacy level. A data steward must make the non-trivial choice of a privacy level that balances the requirements of users and the monetary constraints of the business entity.

arxiv-2012-05781.title: Quantum theory is exclusive: a distributed computing setup
arxiv-2012-05781.creator: Sutapa Saha, Tamal Guha, Some Sankar Bhattacharya, Manik Banik
arxiv-2012-05781.description: Abstract The framework of distributed computing, consisting of several spatially separated input-output servers, has immense importance in distant data manipulation. One of the most challenging parts of this setting is to optimize the use of information transmission lines among distant servers.

arxiv-2104-14141.title: On ( i ) (i) -Curves in Blowups of ℙ r \mathbb{P}^{r}
arxiv-2104-14141.creator: Olivia Dumitrescu, Rick Miranda
arxiv-2104-14141.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Olivia Dumitrescu, Rick Miranda. In this paper we study ( i ) (i) -curves with i ∈ { − 1 , 0 , 1 } i\in\{-1,0,1\} in the blown up projective space ℙ r \mathbb{P}^{r} in general points. The notion of ( − 1 ) (-1) -curves was analyzed in the early days of mirror symmetry by Kontsevich with the motivation of counting curves on a Calabi-Yau threefold.

arxiv-2109-09168.title: Inner functions of matrix argument
arxiv-2109-09168.creator: and conjugacy classes in unitary groups
arxiv-2109-09168.description: Abstract Denote by \mathrm{B}_{n} the set of complex square matrices of order n , whose Euclidean operator norms are <1 . Its Shilov boundary is the set \operatorname{U}(n) of all unitary matrices. A holomorphic map \mathrm{B}_{m}\to\mathrm{B}_{n} is inner if it sends \operatorname{U}(m) to \operatorname{U}(n) .

arxiv-2203-12235.title: Geometry-Aware Supertagging with Heterogeneous Dynamic Convolutions
arxiv-2203-12235.creator: Konstantinos Kogkalidis, Michael Moortgat
arxiv-2203-12235.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Konstantinos Kogkalidis, Michael Moortgat. The syntactic categories of categorial grammar formalisms are structured units made of smaller, indivisible primitives, bound together by the underlying grammar’s category formation rules. In the trending approach of constructive supertagging, neural models are increasingly made aware of the internal category structure, which in turn enables them to more reliably predict rare and out-of-vocabulary categories, with significant implications for grammars previously deemed too complex to find practical use.

arxiv-2212-14420.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Peter Ozsváth, Zoltán Szabó. The aim of this paper is to identify the pong algebra defined in our earlier work with a certain endomorphism algebra in the wrapped Fukaya category of the symmetric product of a disk. Introduction In [ 17 ] , we introduced a differential graded algebra, the pong algebra , which is an enrichment of the strands algebra from [ 12 ] .

arxiv-2302-10233.title: Motion of a spinning particle under the conservative piece of the self-force is Hamiltonian to first order in mass and spin
arxiv-2302-10233.creator: Francisco M. Blanco, Éanna É. Flanagan
arxiv-2302-10233.description: Abstract We consider the motion of a point particle with spin in a stationary spacetime. We define, following Witzany Witzany et al. 2019 and later Ramond Ramond 2022 , a twelve dimensional Hamiltonian dynamical system whose orbits coincide with the solutions of the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations of motion with the Tulczyjew-Dixon spin supplementary condition, to linear order in spin.

arxiv-2406-09764.title: MKIDGen3: Energy-Resolving, Single-Photon-Counting MKID Readout on an RFSoC
arxiv-2406-09764.creator: Jennifer Pearl Smith, John I. Bailey, III., Aled Cuda, Nicholas Zobrist, Benjamin A. Mazin
arxiv-2406-09764.description: Abstract Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) are superconducting detectors capable of single-photon counting with energy resolution across the ultraviolet, optical, and infrared (UVOIR) spectrum with microsecond timing precision. MKIDs are also multiplexable, providing a feasible way to create large-format, cryogenic arrays for sensitive imaging applications in biology, astronomy, and quantum information.

arxiv-2506-13810.title: Bridging Pattern-Aware Complexity with NP-Hard Optimization: A Unifying Framework and Empirical Study
arxiv-2506-13810.creator: Olivier Saidi
arxiv-2506-13810.description: Abstract NP-hard optimization problems like the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) defy efficient solutions in the worst case, yet real-world instances often exhibit exploitable patterns. We propose a novel pattern-aware complexity framework that quantifies and leverages structural regularities—e.g., clustering, symmetry—to reduce effective computational complexity across domains, including financial forecasting and LLM optimization.

arxiv-2511-11575.title: Detecting Statistically Significant Fairness Violations in Recidivism Forecasting Algorithms*
arxiv-2511-11575.creator: Animesh Joshi
arxiv-2511-11575.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Animesh Joshi. Machine learning algorithms are increasingly deployed in critical domains such as finance, healthcare, and criminal justice [1]. The increasing popularity of algorithmic decision-making has stimulated interest in algorithmic fairness within the academic community. Researchers have introduced various fairness definitions that quantify disparities between privileged and protected groups, use causal inference to determine the impact of race on model predictions, and that test calibration of probability predictions from the model.

arxiv-2602-10351.title: Superconductivity in strongly correlated systems for local repulsive interactions
arxiv-2602-10351.creator: Humberto M. Silva 1, Francisco Dinóla Neto 2, Griffith M. A. R. 2, Minos A. Neto 2, Octavio D. R. Salmon 2, Mucio A. Continentino 3, Amos Troper 3
arxiv-2602-10351.description: Abstract The understanding of the mechanisms responsible for superconductivity in strongly correlated systems is an interesting and important subject in condensed matter physics. Several theoretical proposals were considered for these systems. The Coulomb interaction between electrons allow a new approach to study this problem.

pmc-10669551.title: A Systematic Review of Deep-Learning Methods for Intracranial Aneurysm Detection in CT Angiography
pmc-10669551.creator: Žiga Bizjak, Žiga Špiclin, Brandon Lucke-Wold
pmc-10669551.description: Background: Subarachnoid hemorrhage resulting from cerebral aneurysm rupture is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality. Early identification of aneurysms on Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA), a frequently used modality for this purpose, is crucial, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithms can improve the detection rate and minimize the intra- and inter-rater variability.

pmc-10835545.title: Mindscapes of Neurorehabilitation: Insights from the European Congress on Neurorehabilitation 2023 – Part I

pmc-10835545.description: efforts from diverse disciplines with an integrated top-down and bottom-up perspective. The synergy of technology and traditional techniques ensures that the patient receives the best possible care. Throughout the years, the European Federation for Neurorehabilitation (EFNR) has developed an impressive network of European neurorehabilitation societies, summing up 24 member societies that represent the organization's backbone.

pmc-11288047.title: North–south pathways, emerging variants, and high climate suitability characterize the recent spread of dengue virus serotypes 2 and 3 in the Dominican Republic
pmc-11288047.creator: Isaac Miguel, Edwin P Feliz, Robinson Agramonte, Pedro V Martinez, Carlos Vergara, Yvonne Imbert, Lucia De la Cruz, Nurys de Castro, Odalis Cedano, Yamilka De la Paz, Vagner Fonseca, Gilberto A Santiago, Jorge L Muñoz-Jordán, Armando Peguero, Robert Paulino-Ramírez, Nathan D Grubaugh, Ana Maria Bisp
pmc-11288047.description: BackgroundDengue fever remains a significant public health challenge in tropical and subtropical regions, with its transmission dynamics being influenced by both environmental factors and human mobility. The Dominican Republic, a biodiversity hotspot in the Caribbean, has experienced recurrent dengue outbreaks, yet detailed understanding of the virus's transmission pathways and the impact of climatic factors remains limited.

pmc-11301696.title: FAST (fast analytical simulator of tracer)-PET: an accurate and efficient PET analytical simulation tool
pmc-11301696.creator: Suya Li, Mahdjoub Hamdi, Kaushik Dutta, Tyler J Fraum, Jingqin Luo, Richard Laforest, Kooresh I Shoghi
pmc-11301696.description: Objective. Simulation of positron emission tomography (PET) images is an essential tool in the development and validation of quantitative imaging workflows and advanced image processing pipelines. Existing Monte Carlo or analytical PET simulators often compromise on either efficiency or accuracy.

pmc-11357941.title: Study of resistance mechanism of Alternaria blight (Alternaria brassicicola) by biochemical markers in Indian Mustard (Brassica juncea L. Czern. &Coss.)
pmc-11357941.creator: Anurag Mishra, Nawaz Ahmad Khan, Ratnesh Kumar Jha, Tamilarasi Murugesh, Ashutosh Singh
pmc-11357941.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) is an important oilseed crop in India. Alternaria leaf spot (Alternaria blight) is incited by the fungus Alternaria brassicicola. It majorly affects crop production leading to a yield loss of up to 70%. To circumvent this problem, the study of the resistance mechanism and identification of biochemical markers is one of the important strategies for its management.

pmc-11468296.title: FTO mediates the diabetic kidney disease progression through regulating the m6A modification of NLRP3
pmc-11468296.creator: Qiang Li, Shujuan Mu
pmc-11468296.description: BackgroundThe objective of our research was to investigate the specific mechanism of FTO in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) progression.MethodsThe DKD model was established with renal tubular epithelial HK-2 cells and mice in vitro and in vivo. The N6-methyladenosine (m6A) content in cells was detected using dot plot assay and the m6A levels of NLRP3 was detected with the MeRIP assay.

pmc-12595605.title: Diagnostic Test Accuracy of Apparent Diffusion Coefficient in Evaluation of Breast Cancer Lymph Node Metastasis: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-12595605.creator: Amirmohammad Azizzadeh, Fahimeh Zeinalkhani, Peyman Kamali Hakim, Aida Mousavi
pmc-12595605.description: AimsThis study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) derived from diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) for detecting lymph node metastasis in breast cancer.MethodsA systematic review and meta‐analysis was conducted following the PRISMA‐DTA guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, PROQUEST, and EMBASE were searched.

pmc-13018745.title: A single harmonised pharmacy process to improve clinical trial set-up times
pmc-13018745.creator: Miriam Lettieri, Sophia Boydell, Andreea Chivu, Sarah Fallon, Andrew Ustianowski, Monika Cien, Claire Cole, Sophia Burgess, Carolyn Davies, Claire Keatley, Anne-Marie Peers, Maxine Syme, Deborah Sutton, Nicola Hermitage, Lydia Sutherland, Michelle Beecroft, Ali Aghabeigi, Beatriz Duran Jimenez
pmc-13018745.description: The UK has fallen from fourth to 10th place in the global ranking for clinical trial activities in the past 6 years. Due to the limited capacity of the clinical trial pharmacy workforce and delays in providing pharmacy approvals, pharmacy has been identified as one of the constraining services that delays the set-up and delivery of clinical trials.

pmc-13020456.title: Giant Biatrial Myxoma With Few Symptoms—The Odd Between the Rare: A Case Report
pmc-13020456.creator: Jeton Bytyci, Dragos Andrei Duse, Marcus ten Hoevel, Karsten Meuter, Dina Borcean, Alexander Albert, Reinhard Hoeltgen, Marcus Wieczorek, Ralf Erkens
pmc-13020456.description: Cardiac myxomas are rare and mostly benign. Their thrombogenic surface can lead to embolization, and their size can impair cardiac hemodynamics. Here, we present a unique case of large biatrial myxomas despite mild symptomatology. A female patient (62 years, Caucasian) presented with aggravation of dyspnea and palpitations, with the first occurrence only four months prior to the current clinical presentation.

pmc-13198975.title: Divide and Cluster: The DIVINE Framework for Deterministic Top-Down Analysis of Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
pmc-13198975.creator: Jherome Brylle Woody Santos, Lexin Chen, Ramón Alain Miranda-Quintana
pmc-13198975.description: We present DIVIsive N-ary Ensembles (DIVINE), a deterministic, top-down clustering framework designed for molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. DIVINE constructs a complete clustering hierarchy by recursively splitting clusters based on n-ary similarity principles, avoiding the need for O(N2) pairwise distance matrices.

pmc-13356755.title: Stable yet shifting: Early toxin dynamics in typical and atypical clownfish–anemone symbioses
pmc-13356755.creator: J Macrander, A Bennett, K Statile, W Rudd, C Tolman, S Kuklina, S Burg, L Whitton, G Langford
pmc-13356755.description: Among venomous animals, cnidarians represent the oldest metazoan lineage in which venom production and a specialized delivery system are defining synapomorphies. Cnidarians also represent the only venomous lineage for which mutualistic symbioses have evolved resulting in scenarios where mutualistic symbionts may also be targets of their venom.
